CIN.stands_in_for: every capacitance on the input rail as one ideal capacitor at the low end of its tolerance, with no ESR and no ESL - the reservoir is an electrolytic whose ESR the omission of makes the dip shallower than it is

RBLOCK.stands_in_for: the reverse-blocking device as its datasheet on-resistance at the gate drive its clamp gives it; it sits in the return, which is where this element sits too

RFIELD.stands_in_for: all four field outputs at their rated current at once, as one resistance sized at the declared input minimum

RFUSE.stands_in_for: the resettable fuse at its maximum resistance one hour after reflow

RLOGIC.stands_in_for: the converter's input draw as a fixed resistance at the bounded maximum

RVIA.stands_in_for: every via the field supply's copper crosses, as one resistance bounded from the board's declared thickness, drill and an assumed plating; the traversal prices the tracks and states that it prices no barrel, so without this the deck would carry less resistance than the board does

RWIRE.stands_in_for: the supply and its wiring as the declared budget; a stiffer supply drops less

SUPPLY.stands_in_for: the external supply at the bottom of the declared input range, as an ideal source

SWITCHON.stands_in_for: the instant every output is enabled together, as an ideal switch; firmware that staggers them sees less than this

description: every field output turns on at once at its rated current, with the field supply's own copper between the fuse and the contact taken from the routed board

basis.detail: the deck carries at least the resistance the board does - the traced copper plus a bounded barrel for every via it crosses - and this network's contact voltage falls as that resistance rises, so the board cannot hold the contact lower than this deck does. The monotonicity is an argument about this circuit rather than a template the tool checks, which is why the basis is assumed

name: field_outputs_switching_on_together_post_layout
